title: devkit-observability-canvas-query-cost-and-trace-schema
content:
Summary:

This is a working canvas intended to steer a small pilot for lightweight observability in Redwood developer devkits (local and ephemeral dev environments). The goal is to provide developers with high-fidelity debugging signals that mirror production token-serving flows while bounding query/trace costs and avoiding noisy telemetry that overwhelms dashboards. This doc covers: metric naming and minimal definitions, a compact trace enrichment schema for tokenized inference calls, dashboard widget patterns optimized for local/devkit use, a simple query-cost model and guardrails, pilot rollout steps, and open questions.

Why this is different / motivation:
- Devkits are the first place engineers iterate on prompts, evaluate models, and reproduce customer issues. Current production-centric observability surfaces too much data and high query cost for local runs.
- We need a consistent mapping from devkit signals to production signals so that investigations can jump from a devkit trace to production traces with minimal mental translation.
- Provide slices that are cheap to compute and cheap to query (pre-aggregated, low-cardinality) and a simple sampling budget for traces.

Goals and success criteria (pilot):
- Developers can get a representative end-to-end trace for a devkit request within 5s of request completion 90% of the time.
- Dashboard panels for devkit runs should render in <2s under a warm cache.
- Per-month query cost for devkit telemetry (observability product billback) is limited to a notional $300 during pilot.
- When a devkit trace points to a cache-miss or kernel fallback, developers can reproduce the same cause in production with an automated mapping.

Scope (what this pilot covers):
- Instrumented runtimes: local dev container (devkit node), dev-staging serving pool (small scale).
- Signals: request/response latency, token counts, KV-cache hit/miss, prefix-match counts, model variant, quantization path, small trace payload (no raw prompts persisted by default).
- Not in scope: full request/response persistence, PII extraction, long-term retention beyond 7 days for devkit data.

Metric definitions (compact canonical list for devkits):
- devkit.request.count: count of inference requests originating from the devkit (unit: requests)
- devkit.request.latency.ms.p50/p95/p99: latency from SDK send to final token emitted (unit: ms)
- devkit.tokens.generated: tokens emitted per request (unit: tokens)
- devkit.kv.cache_hit_rate: ratio hits/(hits+misses) for prefix/KV cache observed during request (unit: fraction)
- devkit.kv.prefetch_count: number of prefetch attempts per request (unit: integer)
- devkit.model.variant: string tag (e.g., gptj-tilt/quantized-v2) used as label, NOT a metric; for panels use limited variant set to keep cardinality low
- devkit.kernel.path_fallbacks.count: increments when runtime uses fallback kernels / slow-paths (unit: count)
- devkit.error.rate: percentage of requests returning non-2xx or internal-runtime-error labels (unit: fraction)
- devkit.qcost.estimated: estimated query cost bucket (low/medium/high) derived from tokens and runtime path; used for billing guardrails (unit: string label)

Metric labeling guidance (cardinality control):
- Allowed labels: environment={devkit,dev-staging}, team={frontend,serving-integration}, model_variant (whitelist), tenant=optional (only in dev-staging), cache_tier={local,prefix,kvcache}
- Avoid high-cardinality labels (user_id, full_prompt_hash) for devkit metrics. Use sampled mapping in traces only.

Trace enrichment schema (compact; designed for sampling & fast decoding):
- trace_id: opaque uuid (indexed)
- span_id parent_span_id: standard tracing anchors (indexed)
- sampled_flag: boolean (decision made by local sampling policy)
- session_id: devkit session id (maps to developer workspace)
- request_shard: devkit node id or ephemeral pod name
- model_variant: limited whitelist string
- token_count: integer
- prefix_kv_hits: integer
- cache_miss_reason: enum {cold, eviction, invalidation}
- kernel_path: enum {fastpath, slowpath, fallback-64bit, fallback-custom-kernel}
- cpu_gpu_affinity: enum {cpu, gpu, mixed}
- runtime_backpressure_ms: integer (sum of internal queueing delays)
- minimal_error_code: short string for quick filters (e.g., KVCACHE_TIMEOUT)
- pseudo_prompt_tag: short tokenized hash (not raw prompt) for developer to map locally

Sampling policy for devkit traces (to hit cost target):
- deterministic capture for any request where kernel_path != fastpath OR cache_miss_reason != cold; this ensures we capture anomalous runtime behavior.
- probabilistic capture for routine requests: 2% sampling in dev-staging, 10% sampling in local devkit (higher for local to aid debugging).
- burst cap: local devkit caps traces to 50 traces/day per developer session and drops low priority samples when exceeded (emit metric devkit.trace.drop_reason).

Dashboard patterns for devkit UX (fast, low-cost):
- Home tile: small sparkline grid (4 panels): request rate, p95 latency, KV cache hit rate, kernel fallback rate. Each panel queries 1m aggregates for last 60m.
- Request inspector: single-request drill down that links to trace_id and a small JSON blob (no raw prompt). The inspector should use a direct CDN cache of recent traces for immediate access (TTL 5m).
- Cost guard: widget that displays estimated devkit query-cost burn by team (daily estimate, rolling 7d). Provide one-click toggle to turn sampling off for the user's local devkit.
- Lightweight timeline: show token flow histogram (tokens emitted per 500ms buckets) derived from pre-aggregates; avoid full token-level logs in dashboard.

Query cost model & guardrails (simple):
- Cost per devkit query = base_query + per_token_rate + fallback_penalty. Notional numbers (pilot): base_query $0.0003, per_token $0.00002, fallback_penalty $0.001 per fallback kernel event.
- Daily budget enforcement: if a team exceeds 80% of daily budget, temporarily reduce devkit sampling to 1% for that team.
- Billing label: devkit.qcost.estimated computed at ingestion and used to pool queries for chargeback.

Implementation notes & small SQL/Flux snippets (illustrative):
- Pre-aggregation example: INSERT INTO metrics_devkit_1m SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) AS minute, env, model_variant, count(*) as requests, quantile(0.95, latency_ms) as p95_latency FROM raw_devkit_requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY minute, env, model_variant;
- Trace filter example (pseudo): SELECT trace_id, token_count, kernel_path FROM traces WHERE env='devkit' AND kernel_path!='fastpath' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 100;

Pilot rollout plan (6 weeks):
- Week 0: Finalize metric names + tracing schema. PR for SDK instrumentation (github PR 87).
- Week 1–2: Implement ingestion pre-aggregators + sampling policy in dev-staging. Run smoke tests.
- Week 3: Release devkit dashboard template to a small alpha group (frontend and solutions-eng). Monitor query-cost and adjust sampling.
- Week 4–5: Gather feedback, patch privacy flags (ensure no raw prompts in stored blobs), add drop metrics and guardrails.
- Week 6: Decide go/no-go and handoff to broader onboarding if stable.

Acceptance criteria for pilot success:
- Devkit dashboard median render time <2s (measured over 100 requests).
- Trace retrieval latency for captured traces <5s for 90% of attempts (using CDN caching).
- Query-cost under pilot cap ($300/month) after 2 weeks of steady use; or have a documented plan to bring it under cap before broader rollout.
- No PII leakage incidents; audit completed.

Open questions / risks:
- How tightly should devkit model_variant labels mirror production model variants? More variants = higher cardinality. Proposal: maintain a whitelist and a fallback label 'other'.
- Retention: 7d seems reasonable for devkit flows but may hamper investigating flakiness across a full development week. Consider rolling retention extension on demand (manual export).
- Developer ergonomics: are toggles to increase local sampling necessary vs. short-lived manual tracing mode? Risk of abuse raising cost.
- Integration with existing operator dashboards: ensure devkit signals are not polluting operator SLO panels.

Next steps (action items):
- Ravi: land SDK instrumentation PR (ENG-5123) and add sampling toggle endpoint (target 2026-03-01).
- Leah: prototype dashboard template and CDN-backed trace cache (target 2026-03-08).
- Marcus: compute conservative query-cost estimator and add early guardrail (target 2026-03-05).
- Ava (owner): schedule 30m alpha review for 2026-03-10, invite frontend, serving-runtime, solutions-eng, and security.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact: emphasis on low-cardinality metrics, minimal traces, and pre-aggregates to keep dashboard interactivity snappy. Expect several follow-up decisions around cardinality and retention.
- Please flag SDK surface concerns (what is easy vs. invasive to add into devkit) and privacy concerns (prompt handling).

Revision history:
- 2026-02-10: initial draft (Ava).
- 2026-02-25: added sampling policy and metric list (Leah).
- 2026-03-05: updated rollout schedule and added cost model (Marcus).

End of canvas.
